editorial.headline: Nationally Open, but Bali Stops This Consumer-Electronics Repair Activity
editorial.standfirst: This consumer-electronics repair activity is open nationally to full foreign ownership, but Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium stops registration there today.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this consumer-electronics repair and maintenance activity through PMA in Bali today. That conclusion is not softened by the national position: the activity is marked TERBUKA nationally, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. The distinction is central for anyone deciding where to place the business. National openness describes the national investment setting; Bali supplies a separate, binding local result for PMA registration. Read together, the two positions give a clear answer: national eligibility does not itself secure a Bali registration.

The activity itself is practical and defined by the equipment it services. It covers repair and maintenance of television and radio receivers, with antenna installation expressly included. Audio and video players are within scope, alongside video cameras made for home users and video-game devices. These are not stray examples: they describe consumer electronics across reception, playback, home recording and gaming. The common thread is the service of repairing and maintaining the stated equipment, with the examples establishing the working perimeter of the activity.

Registration is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. The record therefore presents the activity across the full set of listed scales, while preserving its particular Bali risk finding at the Besar scale. For national PMA purposes, foreign ownership may reach the stated 100% ceiling. Its cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain terms, national PMA treatment permits foreign ownership up to that declared ceiling; it does not answer the separate question of whether Bali will register the activity.

Bali is where the answer changes. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. The stated reason says that, at Besar scale, the OSS risk is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah across every scope. That finding places the activity within Bali’s province-wide, permanent moratorium for PMA registration, recorded as taking effect in May 2026. The practical result is straightforward: a nationally open, fully foreign-ownable consumer-electronics repair business still cannot be registered through PMA in Bali. The national ceiling remains a national fact; it does not displace the Bali block.
